canonical_data: SQL-backed session history (SQLite by default), versioned file artifacts, and agent cards and task messages carried on the Solace event broker
current_repo_note: The README opens with "Solace Agent Mesh in Python is now deprecated" and says it "won't receive new features, bug fixes or security updates"; the repository is archived on GitHub and the last release is 1.28.8 on 2026-08-28. The maintainer points to a rewritten Solace Agent Mesh and a desktop edition that the Atlas does not publish, so there is no superseded_by target.
strengths: Agents discover and delegate to each other as A2A peers over the broker, and a DAG executor runs prescriptive workflows with agent, switch, loop and map nodes

The model layer goes through LiteLLM, so OpenAI, Azure, Vertex, Bedrock, Anthropic and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint are documented configurations, and the same agents are reachable through REST, web chat and Slack gateways
Sessions persist to SQL by default and artifacts are versioned files, so long conversations survive restarts and large outputs stay out of the model context
weaknesses: The maintainer has stopped the project: the Python version gets no features, fixes or security updates, and its replacement is a separate product the repository does not contain

Running it needs a Solace event broker (an in-memory broker only in a development mode), and the repository documentation presents SSO, RBAC and the visual agent builder as features of a separate Enterprise edition
The only confirmation step found in the built-in tools is the confirm_delete flag on artifact deletion, so approval of other tool calls is left to the operator's design
why_it_matters: A production-minded reference for brokered, A2A-based multi-agent systems, now useful mainly as a record of that design and as a migration source for the rewritten product.
